what im specifically analyzing is how masculinity and, necessarily, race impacted 3 male characters
rochester (who is actually never named rochester in wide sargasso sea, hes given back his name for ease of analysis but its very intentional that he was stripped of his name when he is the one who steals bertha mason (the protagonists) birth name of antoinette as a form of power/control over her) is a european man who essentially is driven mad by his time in jamaica. he is a body out of place as he is not respected as he believes he should be as a white man and watches as other characters, specifically black female characters, maintain a similar positoning he believes He should inhabit

author: slayc127
content: daniel is a mixed race black man who is constantly striving for whiteness as it is the only way he believes he can find visibility/class mobility, and despises whiteness because of this. his white father abandoned him and daniel has spent his life trying to achieve a level of respecability that he will never be able to grasp--colonization exists and is supported by the belief non-white people will never be able to achieve 'whiteness'. homi bhabha has written about mimicry and thats why i centered this part on, usually i explain this bit better but for some reason right now it isnt as clear is i wish i culd get it

author: slayc127
content: simone browne (ut austin professor) wrote about racialized surveillance and traced how our modern methods of surveillance (literal security, cameras, biometrics) are predated by methods of surveillance/control used to 'maintain' black slaves. she wrote about how there is no freedom to be found in striving for visiblity in a system built on the belief that non-white bodies are the lowest form of life, to be very direct with it. the character sandi kind of embodies this idea, because he is never directly in the narrative and everything we hear is second hand. while rochester is driven mad by his inability to maintain power in jamiaca and daniel spends the novel fruitlessly seeking visiblity, sandi simply becomes opaque. his justice or i guess peace is derived from his (presumed) disinterest in being seen. he is still a character because none of us can go outside of the system, but does not try to act within them, if that makes sense
